layoutBarrier.statement: Every original payload ends exactly at its short index table. Frozen4080 layout retains this adjacency. Appending slot4080 overwrites metadata, even if more virtual address space exists after Mission.
layoutBarrier.contiguousReserve: A reserve/commit layout needs fixed maximum offsets before Mission construction or comprehensive address interception. It is not an unbounded live-growth solution.
layoutBarrier.segmented: Keep old payload blocks at their addresses. Construct new blocks for all five pools, create wide sidecar metadata, then publish a new immutable directory/capacity epoch. Existing direct Mission+index*stride consumers must be replaced or routed; sidecar allocation alone cannot enable engine access.
layoutBarrier.widths: Original short metadata uses positive capacity+1 sentinel: representable capacity<=32766, current unroll-compatible multiple30<=32760. These are arithmetic bounds, not tested limits. Sidecar64-bit IDs/32-bit metadata still require translation or widening of every native int32 Agent index, short-table, packed/network/replay consumer.

prepare: Validate source identity and ensure engine runtime initialized.
Allocate all payload and metadata segments privately with checked multiplication/alignment.
Run606a20 for both Agent pools and companion initializers; record completed count after each success; then set inactive headers.

On failure reverse-destroy completed Agent elements, free unpublished segments, leave old directories/capacity/live counts unchanged. Do not destroy the element whose constructor failed a second time.
Acquire a proven engine publication barrier, publish all five payload directories and metadata as one epoch, then expose capacity to admission and enumerators.
Keep prior directory versions alive until all readers leave their epoch; never move or destroy existing payload merely to grow.
transaction.stockMutationRisk: 5d8020 increments count and writes header before virtual+68. Explicit5cd130 path writes header before reset then commits table/count. Neither is a general transaction or a thread-safe growth primitive.
transaction.teardown: Replace full-capacity stock destructor/reset/EH loops with constructed-count per segment traversal; retain original removal semantics for live slots. Native callbacks and managed cached pointers must be detached before block release.

directGlobalFieldScope.conclusion: Decoded portions of these direct-global-reference fragments have one task-submission writer, two constructor zero stores and three post-wait clears. Undecoded tails, opaque owner aliases and other routines without directglobal reference remain outside this bounded scan.

nativeTask.waitScope: A task-completion primitive, not a global reader fence. Reentrant/pumped jobs, task completion publication after managed callback, native physics/render readers, and exact safe hook placement still require integration proof.

quiescence.synchronousJobs: 1f2de0 drains its own remaining-work counter before return; fd930 decrements after each worker callback. This proves a particular batch, not absence of all Mission readers.
candidates: After native task wait and reference release in a phase that cannot submit new Mission readers until growth ends.
Explicit engine-integrated reader epoch/exclusive growth barrier around every routed lookup and native job lifetime.
blockers: OnPreMissionTick alone is not proven safe because managed tickCompleted precedes worker-tail callbacks.
No complete native/managed/physics/render reader participation or growth publication protocol is yet established.
Taskwait pumps jobs and consumes a retained reference; a raw call from managed code without exact owner/thread/refcount contract is unsafe.
